turn.user_message: Which automation do we switch on first?
turn.context: From transcript 31 (the first step: read access, then four weeks of measuring) and bed-management.md §7.4.1 and §7.4.2. The last Automations turn: the day on the wards, the people, the team and the measures are only named here.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Automations, turn 7 (the record stops at 31)

text: Two automations switch on first. They need only read access and one billing report.
bullets: Admission steps timed. Each of the five steps is stamped, so paperwork shows apart from waiting.
Dead bed time measured. Bill close against bill open, bed by bed. Your own number, before anything changes.
Then discharge is built, and the bed map on top. That step also changes how the day runs on the wards.
chat.invite: When you are ready, we can look at how the day changes on the wards.
prompts: How does the day change on the wards?
Who needs to agree to this?
How would we know it is working?
chat.pointer: Step through the build. Pick a row to see when it switches on.

blocks.title: Two lamps first, then the rest
blocks.deck: Each row is one automation. Step through the build and watch which lights first.

blocks.hint: Step through the build. Pick a row to see when it switches on.

mains.name: Discharge, automated
mains.line: The bed plan runs on its times

sheets.title: Admission steps timed
sheets.text: Each of the five admission steps is stamped. You see your real 3½ hours, step by step, before anything changes.
sheets.entry: Which admission step feels slowest to you?

sheets.title: Dead bed time, measured
sheets.text: One report joins bill close and bill open against the same bed. Your 4 to 5 hours becomes a number you track weekly.

lines.label: Makes
lines.value: Dead bed time, bed by bed

sheets.title: Discharge times checked
sheets.text: Comes with discharge itself. From here on, the bed side plans on real times.

sheets.title: Who frees a bed, predicted
sheets.text: The four weeks of measuring give it your own stays. It is tested before the bed map uses it.
sheets.entry: How many procedures make up most of your admissions?

sheets.title: Tomorrow’s bed map
sheets.text: Built on top of discharge. A first pass at 2 PM and a freeze at 6 PM, every day.
sheets.entry: How many planned admissions on a usual day?

hand.does: Checks the 6 PM freeze before it goes out.

sheets.title: Call-in times, bed by bed
sheets.text: The last lamp. It needs everything above, because it tells real patients when to come.

lines.label: Needs
lines.value: The bed map and discharge times

sheets.entry: Who should check call-in times at first?

blocks.label: Switched on first
blocks.sub: Both run on read access and one report. Each gives your own number before anything else changes.
